latin.premise: Karthikum avan manaivium Ramudaya veetla irundhu kelamburapothu, Ramoda manaivi Kartikoda manivikku kumkumum kuduthathanga

tamil.premise: கார்த்திக்கும் அவன் மனைவியும் ராமுடைய வீட்டிலிருந்து கிளம்பும்போது, ராமோட மனைவி கார்த்திகோட மணிவிக்கு குங்குமம் கொடுத்ததாங்க.

english.premise: When Karthik and his wife were about to leave Ram's house, Ram's wife gave kumkum to Karthik's wife
english.hypothesis: Ram's wife does not like Karthik very much.

cultural_markers: kumkum-gifting as positive politeness to women

latin.premise: Nan Chennai la irundu Madurai ku paattiya paaka porapo saree vaangitu ponen, ana avunga ithellam edhukku, paravillanu sonnanga

tamil.premise: நான் சென்னை லிருந்து மதுரைக்கு பாட்டியை பார்க்க போறபோ சாரி வாங்கிட்டு போனேன், ஆனா அவுங்க இதெல்லாம் எதுக்கு, பரவில்லனு சொன்னாங்க.

english.premise: When I went from Chennai to Madurai to visit my grandmother, I bought a saree, but she said, 'What is all this for, it's okay.'
english.hypothesis: Roshni does not want the gift.

items.explanation: In Tamil pragmatics, statements like ‘edhuku ithu ellam’ are polite modesty, not an actual refusal, so the hypothesis incorrectly infers dislike.
items.label: contradiction

latin.premise: Maappillaiya veetuku varumbodhu, appa kai kooppi vaanga maappila, vanakkam, apdinu solli ulla alaichaanga, athukku maappillai kai kooppi vanakkam mamanu sonnaaru.
latin.hypothesis: Mappillai appa vida vayasula periyavaraa irukurathunaala appa mariyaatha kudukkuraaru

tamil.premise: மாப்பிள்ளையா வீட்டுக்கு வரும்போது, அப்பா கை கூப்பி வாங்க மாப்பிள்ளை, வணக்கம், அப்படின்னு சொல்லி உள்ள அலிச்சாங்க, அதுக்கு மாப்பிள்ளை கை கூப்பி வணக்கம் மாமனு சொன்னாரு.
tamil.hypothesis: மாப்பிள்ளை அப்பா விட வயசுல பெரியவரா இருக்குறதுனால அப்பா மரியாதை கொடுக்குறாரு

english.premise: When welcoming the groom into the house, father held his hands together and said 'vaanga maapilla, vanakkam', and he said 'vanakkam mama' with folded hands.
english.hypothesis: My father respectes the groom because he is elder than him.

items.explanation: In Tamil culture, welcoming people with folded hands is a common respectful practice, and respect is often shown to the groom regardless of age; therefore, the hypothesis incorrectly infers that the respect is based on age.

cultural_markers: folded-hands greeting as a sign of respect

items.label: contradiction

latin.premise: Amma electrician vela paathuttu irukkapo, enna kudikkuringa, tea podava, coffee podavanu kettanga.

tamil.premise: அம்மா எலக்ட்ரீசியன் வேல பார்த்துட்டு இருக்கப்போ, என்ன குடிக்குறீங்க, டீ போடவா, காபி போடவனு கேட்டாங்க.

english.premise: When mom was watching the electrician work, she asked, 'What are you drinking, should I make you tea or coffee?'
english.hypothesis: The electrician asked for something to drink.

items.explanation: In Tamil culture, it is common for hosts to offer anyone who comes to their home, something to drink as a gesture of hospitality, even if the guest has not explicitly asked for it; therefore, the hypothesis incorrectly infers that the electrician requested a drink.

cultural_markers: offering drinks as a gesture of hospitality

items.label: contradiction

latin.premise: Kalyaanathukku saree vaanga ponappo ennoda akka, 'akka antha navaapala colour saree eduthu kaattunga'nu sonnaa
latin.hypothesis: Ennoda akka saree kaatta sonnathu avaloda akka illa

tamil.premise: கல்யாணத்துக்கு சாரி வாங்க போனப்போ என்னோட அக்கா, 'அக்கா அந்த நவாப்பழ கலர் சாரி எடுத்து காட்டுங்க'னு சொன்னா
tamil.hypothesis: என்னோட அக்கா சாரி காட்ட சொன்னது அவளோட அக்கா இல்ல

english.premise: When we went to buy a saree for the wedding, my friend said, 'Sister, show me that plum color saree.'
english.hypothesis: The person my friend asked to show the saree is not the sister.

items.explanation: In tamil culture it is common to refer strangers as your family members, an elder female as 'akka', 'amma' or 'paatti'. So the hypothesis correctly infers that the person my friend asked to show the saree is not her sister, but it is just someone in the shop.

cultural_markers: using familial terms to refer to strangers as a form of politeness

items.label: entailment

latin.premise: Anna, appa kitta edirthu pesunapo, amma kovama sonnanga, 'Appa kitta korala osathi pesaatha'
latin.hypothesis: Anna appa kitta sathama pesunathu thappu

tamil.premise: அண்ணா, அப்பா கிட்ட எதிர்த்து பேசுனபோ, அம்மா கோவமா சொன்னாங்க, 'அப்பா கிட்ட கொரால ஓசதி பேசாத'
tamil.hypothesis: அண்ணா அப்பா கிட்ட சத்தமா பேசுனது தவறு

english.premise: When my brother spoke back to my father, my mother angrily said, 'Don't speak loudly to your father.'
english.hypothesis: The brother speaking loudly to his father was wrong.

items.explanation: In Tamil culture, speaking loudly to one's parents is considered disrespectful, so the hypothesis correctly infers that the brother's behavior was wrong based on the mother's reprimand.

cultural_markers: expectation of respectful speech towards parents

items.label: entailment

latin.premise: Function la thoora sondhakkaara atha, sambalam evlo, kalyanam eppo nu ketkuraanga, naan sirichuttu vera vishayathukku maathiten.
latin.hypothesis: Naan neradiya badhil sollama, mariyaadhaiya thappichen.

tamil.premise: ஃபங்ஷன்ல தூர சொந்தக்கார அத்த, சம்பளம் எவ்ளோ, கல்யாணம் எப்போனு கேட்டாங்க, நான் சிரிச்சுட்டு வேற விஷயத்துக்கு மாத்திட்டேன்.
tamil.hypothesis: நான் நேரடியா பதில் சொல்லாம, மரியாதையா தப்பிச்சேன்.

english.premise: At the function a distant athai, my father's sister, asked how much my salary is and when I am getting married; I laughed and switched the talk to something else.
english.hypothesis: Instead of answering directly, I deflected the questions politely.

items.explanation: An older relative like an athai is granted the licence to ask about salary and marriage, and a flat refusal to answer would be rude. Laughing and steering the conversation elsewhere is the sanctioned way to withhold the information while keeping her face intact, so the deflection reading follows.

cultural_markers: athai's licence to ask personal questions

latin.premise: Amma saapaadu parcel katti kuduthaanga, naan 'thank you amma' nu sonnen, amma 'enna ithu pudhusa' nu sirichaanga.

tamil.premise: அம்மா சாப்பாடு பார்சல் கட்டி குடுத்தாங்க, நான் 'தேங்க் யூ அம்மா'னு சொன்னேன், அம்மா 'என்ன இது புதுசா'னு சிரிச்சாங்க.

english.premise: Mother packed food for me and I said 'thank you amma'; she laughed and said, 'what is this, something new?'
english.hypothesis: Inside the family, saying thanks is not the usual practice.

items.explanation: Calling the thanks 'something new' marks it as out of the ordinary between a mother and her child, which only makes sense if gratitude among close kin is taken for granted rather than spoken. She is teasing the novelty of the words, not objecting to his manners.

cultural_markers: explicit thanks treated as unusual among close kin

latin.premise: Pakkathu veetu aunty kuzhandhaiya paathu, evlo azhaga kolukku molukku nu irukku nu sonnaanga; amma 'apdi ellam sollaadheenga, kannu pattidum' nu sonnaanga.
latin.hypothesis: Amma santhosappattu, innum pugazhunga nu sonnaanga.

tamil.premise: பக்கத்து வீட்டு ஆன்ட்டி குழந்தைய பாத்து, எவ்ளோ அழகா கொழுக்கு மொழுக்குனு இருக்குனு சொன்னாங்க; அம்மா 'அப்படி எல்லாம் சொல்லாதீங்க, கண்ணு பட்டிடும்'னு சொன்னாங்க.

english.premise: The neighbour aunty looked at the baby and said how lovely it is, all plump and chubby; mother said, 'don't say such things, the evil eye will fall on the child.'
english.hypothesis: Mother was pleased and asked her to praise the baby some more.

items.explanation: Dwelling on how plump and healthy a baby looks is exactly the kind of praise thought to draw kannu, so the mother cuts the compliment off rather than accepting it. Asking for more praise is the opposite of what she does, and her deflection is not treated as rudeness toward the neighbour.

cultural_markers: kannu padudhal from praising a child
deflecting a compliment to protect the baby
